title: Deterministic quota rollback and forensic telemetry for ambiguous reserved-capacity migrations
creator: Anika Patel
description:
Problem:

We have multiple recent incidents where reserved-capacity customers observed token de-duplication and overcharge/noise around daily boundary resets during a migration (reserved->dedicated reallocation) or when replicas rejoined after partition. Root causes seen in postmortems: lost-ack races between gateway and quota-erlang service, non-idempotent counter writes under partial commit, and lack of sufficient forensic telemetry to deterministically reconstruct what happened for billing reconciliation.

Goals:

1) Provide a deterministic, replayable rollback mechanism for tenant quota state when we detect ambiguous transitions during resets, migrations, or failover.
2) Record rich, queryable telemetry events to reconstruct a tenant's quota timeline for the last 30 days for audit/billing.
3) Ensure any rollback/compensation is idempotent, bounded (no unbounded credit creation), and provably consistent across replicas.

Non-goals:

- Replacing existing quota rate-limiter algorithms in this ticket. We focus on correctness/telemetry and safe compensation.

Design proposal (summary):

1) Append-only per-tenant ledger:
   - Each quota mutation (consume, refund, reserve, expire) becomes an append-only ledger entry in the billing-ledger table with a monotonic per-tenant sequence number (seq_no).
   - Entries include: seq_no, event_type, tokens_delta (can be negative), window_anchor (UTC date or rolling window id), origin (gateway id / region), op_id (UUID), prev_seq_hash (for tamper-evidence), and a small JSON metadata blob for context (prompt length, model, route).

2) Two-phase commit for reserved-pool handbacks:
   - When a reserved pool tear-down or migration occurs, we create a two-phase handback operation: a provisional debit + provisional commit marker. Only when commit marker is appended is the change considered finalized. If we detect a partial commit (debit without commit marker) after the event window, the reconciliation worker will issue an idempotent compensating entry to restore state.

3) Deterministic rollback algorithm:
   - Reconciliation worker scans ledger by seq_no range for a tenant and constructs a deterministic prefix-sum. If it finds a gap, duplicate op_id, or out-of-order seq_no from different origins, it emits a deterministic compensating sequence computed by applying the inverse of the offending entries in reverse seq_no order and appending compensation events with a special tag (compensating=true). Compensation entries reference the original op_ids for audit.
   - All compensating entries are bounded by a configurable policy: max_compensate_tokens_per_window and max_compensation_age_days. This prevents unlimited carryovers/credits.

4) Forensic telemetry and query surface:
   - Store a compact timeline per-tenant in ClickHouse for fast queries: seq_no, timestamp, event_type, origin, window_anchor, net_tokens_after, op_id, trace_id.
   - Add an HTTP debug endpoint (internal-only) that returns a signed timeline for last N days and a human-readable reconstruction (CSV) for billing/finance to attach to dispute tickets.

5) Backfill & migration plan:
   - New writes will start producing ledger entries immediately (gateway + quota service change).
   - A backfill job will stream historical counter deltas from the current quota aggregate into the ledger as synthetic entries (tagged synthetic=true) for the last 14 days to enable immediate reconciliation for recent disputes.
   - During migration window, we mark affected tenants with migration_mode=true to make reconciliations stricter and to avoid automatic compensation that would change billed totals without manual review.

6) Safety and idempotency:
   - All ledger appends are idempotent based on op_id. Duplicate writes are ignored. Reconciliation only appends compensations when the ledger state indicates a violation and the op_id is unique.

Observability and metrics:

- New metrics: billing.ledger.append_success, billing.ledger.append_conflict, billing.reconcile.run_count, billing.reconcile.compensations_emitted, billing.reconcile.latency_seconds.
- Dashboards: per-tenant timelines, daily counts of compensations, top 25 tenants with frequent ambiguous ops.
- Alerts: high rate of append_conflict in a region (>= 5/min sustained) and compensations_emitted > threshold (5/day) for a single tenant -> P0 pager.

Rollout plan:

1) Implement safe ledger append in quota service with feature flag (week 1).
2) Start emitting ledger entries for all new quota ops behind flag for small percentage of tenants (week 2).
3) Deploy reconciliation worker in read-only mode (detect-only) and validate deterministic outputs against manual audits (week 3).
4) Enable automatic compensation for non-migration tenants with conservative bounds (week 4).
5) Run backfill for last 14 days for tenants in scope (week 5).
6) Gradually widen scope and tune thresholds (weeks 6-8).

Testing and QA:

- Unit tests for ledger append idempotency, seq_no monotonicity enforcement, and compensation generation.
- Chaos tests: partition gateway-quota interactions and validate reconciliation yields stable final prefix-sums.
- End-to-end billing integ test against staging billing pipeline with synthetic chargeable events.

Open questions / trade-offs:

1) Storage cost vs retention: ClickHouse timeline retention of 30 days is proposed for fast auditing; longer requests will rely on cold storage (S3). Cost estimate to be provided by infra.
2) Two-phase commit complexity: alternative is to accept eventual correction without provisional commits; we chose 2PC to make migration handback explicit and auditable.
3) Operational overhead of manual review mode for migration tenants: need runbook and on-call rotation implications.

Links and artifacts:

- PRD: https://redwood.atlassian.net/l/c/PRD-Quotas-rollback (internal)
- Design doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/quotas/deterministic-ledger (internal)
- Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/14762
- Postmortem that motivated ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/l/c/PM-7892

Acceptance criteria:

- Ledger append implemented and behind flag with idempotency at op_id level.
- Reconciliation worker can generate deterministic compensating sequences in read-only mode; outputs match manual forensic audits for 10 sampled tenants.
- Forensic timeline endpoint returns signed timeline and CSV for a tenant for past 14 days in <= 5s in staging.
- Billing team sign-off on rollback policy and compensation bounds.
